question: When zinc granules react with dilute sulphuric acid, a colourless gas is produced which burns with a ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**pop sound.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hydrogen gas** is developed generally when a metal responds with a corrosive.
 
• At the point when zinc responds with weakened sulphuric corrosive, zinc sulfate, a salt, is shaped with the arrival of hydrogen gas.
 
• When a consuming matchstick is brought close to the test tube containing hydrogen gas,
 
• it puts off the consuming matchstick and produces a **pop strong.**
 
• Hydrogen gas is delivered when zinc is responded with sulphuric corrosive.

** Zn+H 2SO4(aq)→ZnSO4(aq)+H2**​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A gas fire seeming yellow or orange in a variety of acting with pops of yellow or orange shows an ill-advised proportion of **oxygen **for burning.
 
• These green flares are delivered by the discharge of energized copper particles when copper sulfate is added to the copying liquor.
 
• **Red or yellow flares **mean there could be an issue, like fragmented ignition.
 
• This tone is brought about by extremely **fine **ash particles created by the fire, which consumes almost a portion of the temperature it should.
 
• **Pop sound **means the presence of any ignitable gas, which would promptly burst into flames when it is acquired contact with adequate intensity or fire.
